metadata.title: Advancing language education with ChatGPT: A path to cultivate 21st-century digital skills

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This study used a small, classroom-based sample of Iranian high-school English learners (three schools in Tehran area) and administered a researcher-developed questionnaire after integrating ChatGPT into English classes. The methodology does not report any complex survey design, sampling weights, or replicate-weight procedures, and the analysis is conducted using PLS-SEM rather than ILSA-style plausible-value achievement scaling. Because no ILSA microdata sampling frame is used, there is no documented weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) to apply for population-representative inference. Consequently, results should be interpreted as model-based relationships within this convenience sample rather than as weighted estimates for a national or international target population.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The study does not use ILSA-style cognitive achievement outcomes with plausible values; instead, it models latent constructs measured via Likert-scale questionnaire items (e.g., information management, information evaluation, collaboration, communication, critical thinking, creativity, problem-solving). Because the dependent variables are non-PV survey constructs and the paper does not describe any missing-data procedure (e.g., listwise deletion or imputation), missing-data handling is not reported. This is a reporting gap for transparency, but it is not a PV-related omission.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Convenience sample of high-school English learners in Iran (three schools) who were expected to pass the national course book Vision 3 (third year of high school). The teacher integrated ChatGPT into English-class activities and administered the study questionnaire before the final exam; the paper reports total participants (236) and demographic breakdown but does not specify additional inclusion/exclusion criteria beyond participation and the shared English proficiency level.

main_findings.dataset_used: ChatGPT-assisted language learning (Iran, 2023–2024 high-school English classes)
main_findings.performance_metrics: PLS-SEM structural model: R²=0.092; Q²=0.044; SRMR=0.06. Significant paths: none reported as accepted for INFOM (e.g., PER→INFOM β=0.091, p=0.347; ANT→INFOM β=0.097, p=0.146; DSA→INFOM β=-0.107, p=0.156; INT→INFOM β=0.016, p=0.834; ACC→INFOM β=0.212, p=0.001).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ChatGPT-assisted language learning data from Iranian high-school English classes, the study leveraged ChatGPT personalization, anthropomorphism, digital self-authenticity, interactivity, and accuracy/responsiveness to predict information management, finding that only ChatGPT accuracy & responsiveness had a significant positive effect on information management (ACC→INFOM β=0.212, p=0.001) while other features were not significant. This indicates that improving perceived reliability and speed of ChatGPT responses may be more important than personalization or anthropomorphic cues for helping learners organize information during language learning, though causal claims are limited by the cross-sectional self-report design.

main_findings.dataset_used: ChatGPT-assisted language learning (Iran, 2023–2024 high-school English classes)
main_findings.performance_metrics: PLS-SEM structural model: R²=0.230; Q²=0.134. Significant paths accepted: PER→INFOE β=0.334, p=0.000; INT→INFOE β=0.174, p=0.004; ACC→INFOE β=0.142, p=0.031. Rejected: ANT→INFOE β=0.041, p=0.471; DSA→INFOE β=0.003, p=0.969.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ChatGPT-assisted language learning data from Iranian high-school English classes, the study leveraged ChatGPT personalization, anthropomorphism, digital self-authenticity, interactivity, and accuracy/responsiveness to predict information evaluation, finding that personalization, interactivity, and accuracy/responsiveness significantly improved learners’ information evaluation (PER→INFOE β=0.334, p=0.000; INT→INFOE β=0.174, p=0.004; ACC→INFOE β=0.142, p=0.031), while anthropomorphism and digital self-authenticity were not significant. This indicates that instructional designs emphasizing tailored guidance, interactive dialogue, and trustworthy responses may strengthen learners’ ability to judge the usefulness and reliability of AI-provided information, though the evidence is correlational and based on self-reported questionnaire measures.

main_findings.dataset_used: ChatGPT-assisted language learning (Iran, 2023–2024 high-school English classes)
main_findings.performance_metrics: PLS-SEM structural model: R²=0.076; Q²=0.037. Significant paths accepted: INT→DCM β=0.149, p=0.047; ACC→DCM β=0.183, p=0.004. Rejected/not significant: PER→DCM β=-0.017, p=0.824; ANT→DCM β=0.023, p=0.719; DSA→DCM β=0.003, p=0.967.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ChatGPT-assisted language learning data from Iranian high-school English classes, the study leveraged ChatGPT personalization, anthropomorphism, digital self-authenticity, interactivity, and accuracy/responsiveness to predict digital communication skills, finding that only interactivity and accuracy/responsiveness significantly supported digital communication (INT→DCM β=0.149, p=0.047; ACC→DCM β=0.183, p=0.004) while personalization, anthropomorphism, and digital self-authenticity were not significant. This indicates that teachers should prioritize interactive use of ChatGPT and ensure learners perceive responses as accurate and timely when aiming to improve how students communicate AI-generated information to specific audiences, while recognizing that the model explains a modest share of variance (R²=0.076).

main_findings.dataset_used: ChatGPT-assisted language learning (Iran, 2023–2024 high-school English classes)
main_findings.performance_metrics: PLS-SEM structural model: R²=0.118; Q²=0.083. Significant paths accepted: PER→COL β=0.185, p=0.005; ACC→COL β=0.143, p=0.037. Significant negative path rejected: ANT→COL β=-0.237, p=0.000 (rejected). Not significant: DSA→COL β=-0.120, p=0.039 (reported as not significant in results table); INT→COL β=-0.019, p=0.793.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ChatGPT-assisted language learning data from Iranian high-school English classes, the study leveraged ChatGPT personalization, anthropomorphism, digital self-authenticity, interactivity, and accuracy/responsiveness to predict collaborative digital skills, finding that personalization and accuracy/responsiveness positively predicted collaboration (PER→COL β=0.185, p=0.005; ACC→COL β=0.143, p=0.037) while anthropomorphism significantly reduced collaboration (ANT→COL β=-0.237, p=0.000). This indicates that while ChatGPT can support collaborative work when used for tailored and reliable assistance, highly human-like conversational cues may encourage individual reliance and undermine peer collaboration, suggesting the need for teacher-designed collaborative structures and monitoring.

main_findings.dataset_used: ChatGPT-assisted language learning (Iran, 2023–2024 high-school English classes)
main_findings.performance_metrics: PLS-SEM structural model: R²=0.304; Q²=0.218. Significant paths accepted: PER→CRT β=0.232, p=0.000; DSA→CRT β=0.159, p=0.018; INT→CRT β=0.447, p=0.000. Not significant: ANT→CRT β=0.043, p=0.455; ACC→CRT β=-0.062, p=0.357.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ChatGPT-assisted language learning data from Iranian high-school English classes, the study leveraged ChatGPT personalization, anthropomorphism, digital self-authenticity, interactivity, and accuracy/responsiveness to predict critical-thinking digital skills, finding that personalization, digital self-authenticity, and especially interactivity significantly increased critical thinking (PER→CRT β=0.232, p=0.000; DSA→CRT β=0.159, p=0.018; INT→CRT β=0.447, p=0.000), while anthropomorphism and accuracy/responsiveness were not significant. This indicates that fostering interactive dialogue and learners’ perceived authenticity may be more effective for building critical evaluation habits than relying on human-like chat cues or perceived response quality alone, though the study’s self-report design limits causal interpretation.

main_findings.dataset_used: ChatGPT-assisted language learning (Iran, 2023–2024 high-school English classes)
main_findings.performance_metrics: PLS-SEM structural model: R²=0.237; Q²=0.144. Significant paths accepted: PER→CRE β=0.218, p=0.001; DSA→CRE β=0.171, p=0.019; INT→CRE β=0.249, p=0.000; ACC→CRE β=0.147, p=0.028. Not significant: ANT→CRE β=0.078, p=0.188.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ChatGPT-assisted language learning data from Iranian high-school English classes, the study leveraged ChatGPT personalization, anthropomorphism, digital self-authenticity, interactivity, and accuracy/responsiveness to predict creative digital skills, finding that personalization, digital self-authenticity, interactivity, and accuracy/responsiveness all significantly improved creativity (PER→CRE β=0.218, p=0.001; DSA→CRE β=0.171, p=0.019; INT→CRE β=0.249, p=0.000; ACC→CRE β=0.147, p=0.028), while anthropomorphism was not significant. This indicates that well-designed ChatGPT-supported learning experiences that combine tailored support, interactive engagement, and reliable responses can enhance learners’ creative production, though the findings reflect associations in a convenience sample rather than population-level effects.

main_findings.dataset_used: ChatGPT-assisted language learning (Iran, 2023–2024 high-school English classes)
main_findings.performance_metrics: PLS-SEM structural model: R²=0.359; Q²=0.219. Significant paths accepted: ANT→PS β=0.179, p=0.009; INT→PS β=0.379, p=0.000; ACC→PS β=0.254, p=0.000. Not significant: PER→PS β=0.052, p=0.347; DSA→PS β=0.083, p=0.161.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ChatGPT-assisted language learning data from Iranian high-school English classes, the study leveraged ChatGPT personalization, anthropomorphism, digital self-authenticity, interactivity, and accuracy/responsiveness to predict problem-solving digital skills, finding that interactivity, accuracy/responsiveness, and anthropomorphism significantly improved problem-solving (INT→PS β=0.379, p=0.000; ACC→PS β=0.254, p=0.000; ANT→PS β=0.179, p=0.009), while personalization and digital self-authenticity were not significant. This indicates that to cultivate problem-solving competencies with ChatGPT, teachers should emphasize interactive use and ensure learners perceive responses as accurate and timely, while recognizing that human-like conversational cues may help learners engage with problem-solving tasks individually.

data.outcome_summary: This paper investigates how ChatGPT-related features shape Iranian high-school English learners’ self-reported 21st-century digital skills using a questionnaire-based PLS-SEM model (N=236; three schools; 2023–2024). The study does not use ILSA/PISA/ICILS achievement data or machine-learning prediction; instead, it estimates structural relationships among latent constructs representing ChatGPT personalization, anthropomorphism, digital self-authenticity, interactivity, and accuracy/responsiveness, and seven digital-skill outcomes (information management, evaluation, communication, collaboration, critical thinking, creativity, and problem-solving). Key results show significant positive effects of personalization on information evaluation and creativity, interactivity on critical thinking and problem-solving (and also communication/creativity), and accuracy/responsiveness on information management and several other skills, while anthropomorphism reduces collaborative skills but supports problem-solving. Limitations include convenience sampling, gender imbalance, reliance on self-report, and no reported missing-data handling; therefore, causal interpretations are not warranted.
